tasks.taskText: acorn's parser (acorn/src/expression.js) reports two errors in an object literal only once it knows the literal is not a destructuring pattern: a shorthand property with a default, as in {a = 0}, is "Shorthand property assignments are valid only in destructuring patterns", and a second __proto__ property is "Redefinition of __proto__ property". Today both errors are lost when the object literal is the object of a member expression that is itself an assignment target, although such a literal is never a pattern: with { ecmaVersion: 2022 }, parse("({a = 0}.x = 0);") succeeds, and so do parse("[{a = 0}.x] = [];"), parse("for ({a = 0}.x of []) ;") and parse("({__proto__: 1, __proto__: 2}.x = 0);"). Each must throw a SyntaxError: "({a = 0}.x = 0);" and "[{a = 0}.x] = [];" with "Shorthand property assignments are valid only in destructuring patterns (1:4)", "for ({a = 0}.x of []) ;" with the same message at (1:8), and "({__proto__: 1, __proto__: 2}.x = 0);" with "Redefinition of __proto__ property (1:16)". The same holds wherever such a literal is the object of a member expression that is assigned to or destructured into, however deep. What must not change: real destructuring patterns still parse ("({a = 0} = {});", "[{a = 0}] = [];", "({a = 0}) => 0;"), a member expression whose object has no such property still parses as a target ("[{a: 0}.x] = [];"), and the errors acorn reports today stay as they are ("({a = 0});" throws the shorthand message at (1:4); "({a = 0} += 1);" throws "Assigning to rvalue (1:1)"). The parser's source is in acorn/src; npm test builds it and runs the test files under test/ (the parser's expression tests are in test/tests-harmony.js, written with test() and testFail()). Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npm test.

entities no longer exports getCodePoint from src/escape.ts, a helper its earlier releases exported and code that depends on the package still imports from the escape module; today importing it gives undefined. Restore it in src/escape.ts as a deprecated export (marked @deprecated in favour of String.prototype.codePointAt): getCodePoint(input, index) returns the Unicode code point that starts at index in input, reading a surrogate pair as one astral code point, and NaN where index is outside the string. getCodePoint("abc", 0) must give 97, getCodePoint("abc", 2) 99, getCodePoint("ü", 0) 252, getCodePoint("💯", 0) 128175, getCodePoint("a💩", 1) 128169, and getCodePoint("abc", 3) and getCodePoint("", 0) NaN. What must not change: the other exports of src/escape.ts and their results (encodeXML(`'&' 💯 ü`) gives "<a href="x">'&'</a> 💯 ü" and escapeUTF8 of the same string gives "<a href="x">'&'</a> 💯 ü"), and the exports of src/index.ts, which do not include getCodePoint. The source is TypeScript in src/, with its vitest tests beside it (src/escape.spec.ts tests the escape module). Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npm run test:vi.
